messages:
elaine: heads-up — customer (AcmeAnalytics) opened a ticket: after a regional outage their chat stream started returning malformed tokens + occasional 400s. They say it was fine until failover kicked in. request_id=rq_0a1b2c3d

kevin: can you paste one of the error responses? 400 or 422?

essie: (note: placeholder name corrected to original 'elaine')

elaine: 400. response snippet: `{ \"error\": \"tokenizer error: unknown token id 50256\", \"request_id\": \"rq_0a1b2c3d\" }`

olivia: that sounds like a tokenizer mismatch — usually when fallback picks a variant with a different tokenizer/config. Which model did they request?

elaine: they called `model=redwood-r50` in us-east-1. The routing log shows: `route -> us-east-1 (capacity low) -> fallback -> eu-west-1:r50-quant-pruned-v1` (quantized variant).

ops-bot: routing-decision: {"request_id":"rq_0a1b2c3d","origin_region":"us-east-1","selected_region":"eu-west-1","model":"r50-quant-pruned-v1","reason":"fallback_capacity"}

kevin: ah ok. `r50-quant-pruned-v1` was onboarded with a different tokenizer (vocab v2) during last quant rollout — incompatible token ids. That would cause the unknown token id errors.

olivia: customer also reported cross-region latency spikes after the reroute. They're hitting 700-900ms p50 for streaming start.

elaine: customer repro steps I have: 1) set region=us-east-1, model=redwood-r50 2) send `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"Hello there"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=redwood-r50` 3) sometimes fails with tokenizer error when failover triggers.

kevin: quick triage I ran: fetched serving trace for rq_0a1b2c3d: `trace: prefer_region=us-east-1 -> scheduled to us-east-1/g1 -> capacity exhausted -> fallback_policy=allow_any_variant -> selected eu-west-1/r50-quant-pruned-v1`.

kevin: root cause: fallback_policy `allow_any_variant` is too permissive; it doesn't check `tokenizer_compatibility` flag in model registry metadata. When a quantized variant was chosen, tokenizer drift caused 400s and semantic drift.

olivia: reproduction confirmed in staging when I force failover: curl command + simulate capacity saturation -> same 400 token errors and streaming delayed due to cross-region RTT.

elaine: customer is asking for an immediate mitigation — they can't tolerate changed outputs.

kevin: mitigation options (short term):
- pin their account to `model=redwood-r50@vX` (explicit version) so routing won't substitute variant
- or update tenant routing policy to `fallback_policy=regional_only` or `fallback_restrictions=tokenizer_compatible_only`

olivia: which is fastest?

kevin: pinning model version is fastest (single API flag on the tenancy). I'll prepare the patch.

ops-bot: support-ticket-update: ticket#S-4829 assigned to kevin. SLA: P1 - customer-facing loss of output integrity.

elaine: I've told the customer we'll pin their calls to the requested version and follow up about a permanent fix. They want a timeline.

kevin: plan (actionable):
1) short-term (15m): pin customer to `redwood-r50@2026-11-02` via account override — prevents variant substitution. (owner: kevin)
2) short-term (30m): add a routing hotfix to block fallbacks that are tokenizer-incompatible. This is a config change in routing service: `require_tokenizer_compat=true` (owner: sanjay)
3) medium-term: update model registry metadata to include `tokenizer_hash` and have consistency checks in rollout pipelines (owner: ml-onboard)
4) postmortem + release notes (owner: support)

sanjay: I can push the routing hotfix — small change, tests local. Will do canary in staging then prod. ETA 45m.

kevin: done pinning for S-4829 at 16:12 UTC. Notified customer.

olivia: started canary of `require_tokenizer_compat=true` in us-east-1 routing cluster. Observing for 10m.

elaine: customer confirmed reduced errors immediately after pin. They still see slightly higher latency since requests remain in-region but warmup needed. :thumbsup:

kevin: follow-up notes for infra: we should add a model-variant attribute `compatible_families: [redwood-r50]` and ensure fallback picks same family + tokenizer match. Also surface a clear `fallback_tokens_mismatch` metric in the console so SRE/support can detect.

sanjay: logging improvement: include `tokenizer_hash` in request trace for quick comparison. I'll add that to the trace payload.

olivia: I'll file a short KB article for Support: "What to do when failover selects an incompatible variant" with repro steps, quick pins, and routing flags.

elaine: TL;DR for customer: we pinned your calls to requested model version, rolled a safety check to block tokenizer-incompatible fallbacks, and will do a follow-up to ensure no further surprises. ETA for full rollout of registry + tests: 2 weeks.

kevin: closing loop — will add an incident note and link to ticket S-4829.

ops-bot: incident-log: created incident INC-2026-11-02-07 (region fallback selected incompatible variant)

olivia: anything else?

elaine: not for now. I'll keep this thread updated if the customer reopens.
